item.title: Critiquing SCP-001: When Day breaks
item.content:encoded:
Decided to actually use the account for something on here:

I love the SCP a lot but there's a lot I find a bit…convenient about the SCP.

I'll just go and copy paste this thing I had on my reddit:

"I think my immediate complaint is like

It doesn't actually go into the anomaly?

I heard from a older staff member on the wiki (true story, don't remember his name) after I talked to them online the main point he said wasn't about the anomaly, it was about connections to a person

+ show block
– hide block

Which….I guess is alright?????

My main complaint is the style could have been a lot better (part of the guy going to the site could have been an awesome part 2 instead of going how it did)

If it's a narrative story, I want an actual introduction to the event

What happened to the President of the United states?

What happened to the foundation the DAY it happened

What was the breakdown of society itself like the Day it happened?

If an event happens, I want to know why/what happened (SCP-5000 I don't particularly like even remotely, but it does show a actually timeline of an event conciseively)

It could have very easily been set up as "You turn on news broadcast, event happens yada yada"

Site breach insuses, popular/Not popular SCP's are mentioned

10 mins of dialogue, maybe omnipresent detail about the breakdown of the foundation, etc

then it details the guy trying to go for the site.

Instead we're immediately thrusted 2 years later with little to no context as to what happened, it just reads the file then immediately pushes a lover scene.

We don't get any SCP's mentioned, just "Keters" breaching a site and that's it

What about Cain And Able? What about the Star Eyed child?

What about 343 which is apparently either god/the most powerful reality bender to exist?

We don't get practically anything, just lovers, protagonist makes a mistake, the end"

I think the Concept is a truly terrifying and Unique one, I just can't/Don't like how the SCP is actually written, the concept is amazing but the story fails to intrigue me personally.

8/10 for original concept, 3/10 for story


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
An incredible piece of writing, imo.

The SCP Foundation is always depicted as having complete control over a situation.

Eldritch horror? Just pray a bit and shoot at it and you're fine.

Vengeful god? Ritual or two should handle that.

We lost? Nah, just flood the Earth and rebuild it in a decade or two. Easy peasy.

Earth's gonna die? Just dimension hop!

But with this, the SCP Foundation loses. It happened in a split second and wiped out almost all of the human race. Site-19 goes out with a whimper, not a bang. Reality benders tapped out of the situation and not even other anomalies are safe from it, which just adds to the hopeless feel of the article.

My favorite 001. +1'd.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Praise the Sun!

Wait, no. But I love what you did with the sun itself. Having evolved to huddle together at night and to fear the dark, the sun must by the most universal symbol of safety and bravery humanity has or has ever had. We attribute it holy power, and here you've turned it into the ultimate instrument of decay and eternal hellish mutation.

I love the style, too. If you asked me before I read this is the sort of narration you used to frame the story would work for an SCP (rather than a tale), I would certainly have said no. I don't even understand how, but you've made it work.

A resounding success, and easily worthy of a 001 slot! Thank you!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Aaah, this is one of those articles that I find hard to decide a vote on. On the one hand, it's well-written and effective, but on the other hand there's nothing that really 'pops' about it, no piece of writing that's brilliant, no exquisite twist that sticks with me and no idea so fantastic that I can't help but remember it.

And that's the thing - were this not an 001-proposal, that wouldn't be a problem. An interesting premise, solid writing and execution are easily enough to land an article an upvote. But an 001-proposal, for me, needs to stick with me in some way. It's a special spot, so it needs to be special in some way. And this just doesn't do it for me.

The 'sun as evil' angle is nice, but it isn't exactly new, though usually it's the 'scorched earth' thing that makes it a threat rather than this anomalous effect. However, the feel and intent of the contrasting imagery is still the same, so this doesn't stand out enough for me. The thing about even souls being corrupted by the light doesn't do it for me either, as the 'unable to die' thing has also been done many times, and 'flesh blob assimilation' isn't quite different enough to make this particular take on it stand out either. Finally, while the scare factor of implying that the reader is the personnel discovering the files is well-executed, it was also very telegraphed and pretty predictable. Mind, it's very impressive that it was still hair-raisingly effective in spite of this, but if I can see it coming it doesn't stand out either.

So here's my conundrum - this article is good, even really good since it's easily above average, but at the same time it's an 001-proposal and it doesn't meet my standards for those. So, I'm going with a no-vote. I can't in good conscience downvote an article of this high quality but I don't want to upvote either since I don't believe that serving just 'good food' in a restaurant with 2 Michelin stars is sufficient.

Instead, have this imaginary upvote for the article in and of itself: (+1)
It may not increment the nice number on the page, but know that I did like the article!
